candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance client-needs subcategory (6–12% of items); this item tests health teaching, lifestyle safety, and individualized risk-reduction guidance for chronic illness.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Individualized injury-prevention teaching for clients with seizure disorders
candidate.educational_objective: Promote safe, individualized activity for clients with epilepsy while emphasizing water precautions such as avoiding swimming alone and using appropriate supervision rather than imposing unnecessary blanket restrictions.

options.A: Encourage safe physical activity while individualizing precautions; avoid swimming alone and use appropriate supervision around water
options.B: Avoid all exercise and recreation permanently because any physical activity is unsafe with epilepsy
options.C: Swimming alone is acceptable as long as the client has taken antiseizure medication that day
options.D: No activity-specific safety planning is needed because seizure disorders do not increase drowning or injury risk

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current CDC epilepsy guidance states that most people with epilepsy can live full lives and that safe exercise can benefit physical and mental health. CDC specifically warns that swimming and other water sports can be risky and advises avoiding swimming alone. Current CDC drowning-prevention guidance further recommends the buddy system and one-on-one supervision around water for people with seizure disorders. B imposes an unsupported blanket restriction. C falsely treats medication adherence as eliminating water risk. D contradicts CDC safety guidance.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current CDC guidance directly supports safe physical activity for people with epilepsy while requiring enhanced water-safety precautions, including avoiding swimming alone and using supervision/buddy systems.
candidate.source_document_title: Health and Safety Concerns; Preventing Drowning
candidate.source_locator: CDC 'Health and Safety Concerns' → Exercise and physical activity: exercising safely can benefit physical, mental, and emotional health; swimming and water sports can be risky for people with epilepsy; swimming alone should be avoided; discuss safe activity with the health care provider. CDC 'Preventing Drowning' → Use the buddy system: always swim with a buddy; one-on-one supervision around water is recommended for people with seizure disorders because of drowning risk.
